report.scope:
Measure raw-stress reward repeatability and paired 1N/4N grasp discrimination.

Each of eight frozen conditions is duplicated with only the commanded strong
grip force limit changed. The original approach/lift/slide/weak/release schedule,
arm targets, radii, friction and resets are retained. Intrusive observations
make this a behavioral experiment, never a throughput benchmark.
report.limitations: Raw stress and exposure are uncalibrated reward proxies for two explicitly controlled grip choices. This is numerical repeatability and useful discrimination conditional on the chosen480-tet mesh, actual rigid contact and model/radius assumptions. It does not certify a fracture threshold, physical stress accuracy or complete RL training. Different models can change stress rankings without changing rigid motion. All values and any rejected input remain; intrusive observer timing is excluded from throughput.

figure_contract.section: Material x=0, independently intersect each affine tetrahedron. Exact tensor interpolation to section vertices, then Gouraud display of their von Mises values. No cell merging or smoothing; raw global maxima are retained separately. Shared full section scale, no percentile clipping.
figure_contract.traction: All native positive-area samples, material y/z projection, actual normal traction and physical source marker identities. Projection can overlap opposite-side samples; not a continuum island segmentation.
figure_contract.remaining_QA: Inspect both rendered previews before calling figures final.
